title: The Malignant Thoughts and their Consequences
english: To those who have received [well], he freely grants gifts and accepts their gratitude; but to those hesitating, he hands them over to judges and commands them to be exiled from the city. Since these [thoughts] remain within, and the thoughts turn, immediately the demon of pride stands over, striking continuous lightning through the air of the cell, and sending winged dragons, and, the final evil, working a deprivation of wits. But we, having invited destruction through these thoughts, let us live with poverty with thanksgiving, saying, 'For we brought nothing into the world, nor can we bring anything out manifest that we are able: having food and clothing, let us be content with these' (1 Tim 6:7). Remembering also Paul, saying that the love of money is the root of all evils (1 Tim 6:10).

All the impure thoughts, lingering in us because of the passions, bring the mind down to destruction and perdition; for just as the thought of bread lingers in the one starving because of hunger, and the thought of water in the one thirsting because of thirst, so also the thoughts of possessions and of wealth linger because of greed, and the thoughts of filth, and the shameful thoughts born from filth, linger because of the passions. But even upon the thoughts of vainglory, and upon the other thoughts, it will similarly be revealed. And there is no mind being choked by such things that can stand before God and put on the crown of righteousness.

For he, the thrice-afflicted mind in the Gospels (Matt 22), being struck down by these thoughts, renounced the best of the knowledge of Christ; and again, he who is bound hands and feet, and being cast into the outer darkness, was looking down because of these thoughts at the garment, which the one who invited him had decreed was not worthy of such a wedding.
